n1e96358f7bf.s: In the constant Hoysala–Yadava wars, which Yadava ruler of Devagiri defeated the Hoysalas?
n1e96358f7bf.x: Singhana defeated the Hoysalas; Mahadeva Yadava, by contrast, was defeated by them, and Bhillama was beaten by Veera Ballala II.

n0fb0552724e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Veeragallu (hero stone) found at Neeragunda?
o: It may settle the date of Malik Kafur's death
It was found in Arsikere taluk
It may settle the date of Vishnuvardhana's death
n0fb0552724e.x: The hero stone, unearthed on 28 June 2026 at Neeragunda (Arsikere taluk), may help settle the disputed date of Vishnuvardhana's death, not Malik Kafur's.

n4b4ff0c5162.s: Ganapatideva married Narama and Perama and made their brother Jayapa Gajasahani. Whose daughters were they?
n4b4ff0c5162.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, chief of the elephant forces.

nindian-history-149-2-10.s: Which of the following southern dynasties ruled from Madurai?
nindian-history-149-2-10.x: The Pandyas ruled from Madurai; the Yadavas ruled from Devagiri, the Kakatiyas from Warangal and the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra.

new.s: The name Halebidu, taken after Dwarasamudra was sacked by the Delhi armies, means:
new.x: Halebidu means 'old city'; the name came after the Delhi armies sacked Dwarasamudra.

new.s: Halebid, the modern name of the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra, lies in which district of Karnataka?
new.x: Halebid (Halebidu), the old Dwarasamudra, is in Hassan district, Karnataka; Belur is also in Hassan.

new.s: Which Hoysala figure was an early chief under the Western Chalukyas?
new.x: Nripa Kama II was an early Hoysala chief under the Western Chalukyas; Veera Ballala II later made the Hoysalas independent.

new.s: Narasimha III, in whose reign the Somanathapura temple was built, was defeated by:
new.x: Narasimha III (1254–1295) was defeated by the Pandya Maravarman Kulasekhara.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hoysalas:
1. They became independent by the close of the 12th century.
2. Their rule ended at the beginning of the 14th century.
3. They set up their kingdom in the early 8th century AD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Hoysalas were independent by the close of the 12th century and ended at the beginning of the 14th; they did not set up their kingdom in the early 8th century.

new.s: Which queen of Vishnuvardhana remained a Jain even after his conversion to Vaishnavism?
new.x: Vishnuvardhana's queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain though the king turned Vaishnava under Ramanuja.

new.s: Ramanuja came into the Hoysala kingdom while fleeing the persecution of the:
new.x: Ramanuja had fled Chola persecution into Hoysala land, where he converted Vishnuvardhana to Vaishnavism.

new.s: The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid is dedicated to:
new.x: Hoysaleswara at Halebid is a Shiva temple; the Chennakeshava (Belur) and Keshava (Somanathapura) temples are Vishnu temples.

new.s: In which year did Vishnuvardhana build the Chennakeshava temple at Belur?
new.x: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava temple at Belur in 1117; Hoysaleswara dates to c. 1121 and Somanathapura to 1268.

new.s: The name 'Hoysaleswara' of the Halebid temple means:
new.x: Hoysaleswara means 'Lord of the Hoysalas'; the temple was built in dark schist.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Jakanachari is linked with Belur; Mallitamma with Somanathapura, Madanikas with Belur, and Ketamalla built the Hoysaleswara at Halebid.

new.s: Which sculptor is associated with the Keshava temple at Somanathapura?
new.x: Mallitamma is the sculptor linked with Somanathapura; Ketamalla and Somanatha were builders, and Jakanachari is linked with Belur.

new.s: The star-shaped (stellate) temple plan that peaked under the Hoysalas first began under the:
new.x: The star plan began under the Chalukyas (6th c.) and peaked under the Hoysalas (12th c.); the Kalyani Chalukyas passed on soapstone and star plans.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the UNESCO 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas'?
new.x: The three components are Chennakeshava (Belur), Hoysaleswara (Halebid) and Keshava (Somanathapura).

new.s: Which is the only Shiva temple among the three Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas?
new.x: Hoysaleswara at Halebid is the only Shiva temple of the three; Belur and Somanathapura are Vishnu temples.

new.s: In 1342, the Hoysala king Ballala III was killed at Kannanur by:
new.x: Ballala III was killed in 1342 by Ghiyas-ud-din, Sultan of Madurai, at Kannanur; Hoysala land then passed to Vijayanagara.

new.s: Which Hoysala king was defeated by the Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316?
new.x: Ballala III (1295–1342) beat Yadava Ramachandra's forces in 1305 but was defeated by Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316.

new.s: Devagiri, the Yadava capital, was later renamed Daulatabad by:
new.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Devagiri Daulatabad in 1327 when he shifted his capital there.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Yadavas of Devagiri:
1. They were also called the Seuna Yadavas.
2. They were first feudatories of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas.
3. Their capital Devagiri was founded by Shankaradeva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Seuna Yadavas began as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas; Devagiri was founded by Bhillama V (c. 1187), not Shankaradeva.

new.s: Who was the last ruler of the Yadavas of Devagiri?
new.x: Harapaladeva (1313–1317) was the last Yadava ruler; he was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion.

new.s: The Yadava ruler Jaitugi married which daughter of Ganapatideva to him after releasing him?
new.x: Jaitugi released Ganapatideva in 1199 and married his daughter Somaladevi to him.

new.s: Singhana II released Ganapatideva as a counterweight to Hoysala Veera Ballala II's push into which region?
new.x: Ganapatideva was released to check Veera Ballala II's advance into the Krishna–Tungabhadra region.

new.s: Which record of Ramachandra confirms that Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and held Ganapatideva captive?
new.x: The Paithan copper plate of Ramachandra confirms Jaitugi's killing of Rudradeva and capture of Ganapatideva; the Bidar fort inscription records Rudramadevi's victory.

new.s: Sarngadeva, author of the Sangita Ratnakara, was the court musician of:
new.x: Sarngadeva was court musician of Singhana II, at whose court the astronomer Changadeva also served.

new.s: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by:
new.x: Chakradhar Swami founded the Mahanubhava sect; Dnyaneshwar wrote the Dnyaneshwari.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is correctly matched?
new.x: Lilacharitra, the first Marathi prose, is by Mhaimbhat; Sangita Ratnakara is Sarngadeva's, Dnyaneshwari Dnyaneshwar's and Chaturvarga Chintamani Hemadri's.

new.s: Changadeva, who set up a school at Patan, was the grandson of:
new.x: Changadeva, astronomer at Singhana II's court, was the grandson of Bhaskaracharya and taught his works at Patan.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Hemadri:
1. He was Shrikaranadhipa, head of the secretariat and records.
2. He wrote the Sangita Ratnakara.
3. The style credited to him uses black basalt laid without mortar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Hemadri was Shrikaranadhipa under Mahadeva and Ramachandra, and Hemadpanti style uses basalt with no mortar; the Sangita Ratnakara is Sarngadeva's.

new.s: The first Muslim invasion of the South, in which Alauddin Khalji defeated Ramachandra, took place in:
new.x: In 1296 Alauddin Khalji defeated Ramachandra; the Yadavas became vassals and promised the Ellichpur revenue yearly.

new.s: After the 1296 raid, the Yadavas promised Alauddin Khalji the yearly revenue of:
new.x: Ramachandra promised the revenue of Ellichpur every year but did not send it.

new.s: Which Delhi Sultan killed Harapaladeva in 1317–18, ending the Yadava kingdom?
new.x: Harapaladeva was killed by Mubarak Khalji in 1317–18, ending the kingdom.

new.s: Who were the first overlords of the Kakatiyas?
new.x: The Kakatiyas first served the Rashtrakutas and then the Kalyani Chalukyas; the Magallu grant that first mentions them is an Eastern Chalukya record.

new.s: The Kakatiya emblem was changed from Garuda to Varaha by:
new.x: Prola I changed the emblem from Garuda (Rashtrakuta phase) to Varaha (Kalyani Chalukya phase).

new.s: The Kakatiya clan deity Kakatamma (Kakati Devi) was originally the Jain goddess:
new.x: Kakatamma was the Jain Kushmandini absorbed into Hinduism; 'Kakati' means gourd.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Saiva guru – Kakatiya ruler) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Dhruveshwara Pandita was Mahadeva's guru, not Ganapatideva's; Ganapatideva's Raja Guru was Visvesvara Sivacharya.

new.s: Which Kakatiya ruler wrote the 'Nitisara'?
new.x: Rudradeva (1158–1195) wrote the Nitisara, won independence in 1163 and founded Orugallu.

new.s: Which Kakatiya ruler was the first to come to Hanamkonda?
new.x: The Bayyaram inscription says Beta I was the first Kakatiya to come to Hanamkonda.

new.s: The Kakatiya ruler Prola II was killed by the:
new.x: Prola II was killed by the Velanati Chodas; Rudradeva was later killed by Yadava Jaitugi.

new.s: Which Kakatiya ruler erected a victory pillar at Srisailam?
new.x: Prola II backed Someshwara III, developed Hanamkonda and set up a victory pillar at Srisailam.

new.s: Under the Kalyani Chalukyas, the feudatory Kakatiyas bore the title:
new.x: Before independence in 1163, the Kakatiyas were Mahamandaleswaras under the Kalyani Chalukyas.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (title – Kakatiya ruler) is correctly matched?
new.x: Vikrama Chakri was Beta II's title; Chola Chamuvardhi was Beta I's, Arigajakesari Prola I's and Andhra Deshadhiswara Ganapatideva's.

new.s: The title 'Arigajakesari' belonged to which Kakatiya ruler?
new.x: Arigajakesari was the title of Prola I; Rayagajakesari was Rudramadevi's.

new.s: 'Orugallu', the ancient name of Warangal, means:
new.x: Orugallu means 'single rock'; it is the ancient name of Warangal.

new.s: Under Ganapatideva, the completed capital Orugallu was also called:
new.x: Ganapatideva completed Orugallu and moved the court there, naming it Andhranagari; it became Sultanpur after 1323.

new.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara names which lake?
new.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara names Kolleru Lake (APPSC G2 2017).

new.s: Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to:
new.x: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi of Nellore, not to Ganapatideva.

new.s: Ganapatideva's general who took Divi during the coastal campaign from 1201 was:
new.x: From 1201, Ganapatideva's general Mutyalachaundaraya took Divi in the coastal campaign.

new.s: Which tanks were built by Ganapatideva?
new.x: Ganapatideva built the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks; Kesamudram was Prola I's and Arikesari Samudram Prola II's.

new.s: The Kakatiya port Motupalli ('Mutfili') was visited by Marco Polo in the reign of:
new.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli c. 1287–1290 in Rudrama's reign and praised the ruling queen.

new.s: Rudrama Devi married Veerabhadra, a prince of the:
new.x: Rudrama Devi married Veerabhadra, a Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukya prince; Ganapamba married the Kota chief.

new.s: Rudradeva's victory over the Kalachuri confederacy (Mailagi, Medaraja, Dommaraja) took place in:
new.x: Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy in 1159; independence came in 1163.

new.s: Which Yadava ruler killed the Kakatiya Rudradeva?
new.x: Yadava Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and held Ganapatideva captive.

new.s: Who besieged Warangal in 1310, making Prataparudra a tributary?
new.x: Malik Kafur besieged Warangal in 1310; Ulugh Khan took it in 1323.

new.s: Which Kakatiya feudatory bore the title 'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya'?
new.x: Prasadaditya of the Kayastha family bore Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya and helped Rudrama to the throne; Recherla Rudra was Bharadhureya.

new.s: Chouda Samudram was built by a member of which Kakatiya feudatory family?
new.x: Malyala Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram.

new.s: The Nayankara system of military-feudal land grants was organised under:
new.x: The Nayankara system, in which nayakas held land for keeping troops, was organised under Prataparudra II.

new.s: The Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram was built by Beta I's minister:
new.x: Beta I's minister Naranayya built the Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ramappa temple?
o: It was built by Recherla Rudra in 1213
It is known for floating bricks
It stands on a star-shaped platform
new.x: Ramappa was built by Recherla Rudra in 1213 in Ganapatideva's reign; Krishnadevaraya built the Hazara Ramaswamy temple at Hampi.

new.s: Which inscription gives the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas?
new.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription (1219) of Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister, gives the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.

new.s: The Kakatiya Dharmasagara inscription mentions which musical instrument?
new.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the musical instrument Jalakaranda (APPSC 2019).

new.s: The Draksharama inscription (1158) of minister Inangala Brahmi Reddi records the accession of:
new.x: The Draksharama inscription of 1158 records Rudradeva's accession and calls him Vinaya Bhushan.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mailamba:
1. She was a daughter of Ganapatideva.
2. She issued the Bayyaram tank inscription.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Mailamba issued the Bayyaram tank inscription (1219) but was Ganapatideva's sister, not his daughter.

new.s: One tradition says Harihara and Bukka, founders of Vijayanagara, were treasury officers of:
new.x: One tradition makes Harihara and Bukka treasury officers of Prataparudra II who fled to Kampili after Warangal fell in 1323.

new.s: According to one tradition, after the fall of Warangal in 1323 the Sangama brothers fled to:
new.x: The tradition says Harihara and Bukka fled to Kampili after Warangal fell in 1323.

new.s: Which Kakatiya institution was carried on by the Vijayanagara rulers?
new.x: The Kakatiya Nayankara system was carried on by Vijayanagara.
